name: H200 SXM
notes: Per the H200 datasheet's footnote convention (footnote 2: 'With sparsity'), FP64/FP64 Tensor Core/FP32 are dense figures; TF32/BF16/FP16/FP8/INT8 Tensor Core figures are sparse-only, no independently published dense value -- dense fields for those left null rather than derived. FP6 Tensor Core not applicable (Hopper does not support FP6, introduced in Blackwell). cuda_cores/tensor_cores/sm_count left null: despite thorough searching, NVIDIA has never published H200-specific core-count figures in any official datasheet, product brief, or architecture document -- third-party sites assume H200 reuses H100 SXM5's GH100 die figures (132 SM / 16,896 CUDA cores / 528 Tensor Cores), which is plausible but not an NVIDIA-confirmed H200 figure, so left unpopulated. process_node_nm of 4 (TSMC 4N) IS directly sourced for H200 specifically -- NVIDIA's Hopper architecture page names H200 by product name in the same sentence as the TSMC 4N claim ('Built with over 80 billion transistors using a cutting edge TSMC 4N process... fuel the NVIDIA H200 and H100 Tensor Core GPUs'), which is a stronger citation than the H200 product datasheet itself (which only says 'Based on the NVIDIA Hopper architecture' without restating the process node). release_date of 2023-11-13 is NVIDIA's official H200 announcement at SC23. Memory bandwidth stated as '4.8TB/s' in the main H200 datasheet; the H200 NVL product brief independently states a more precise 4,813 GB/s for the same underlying HBM3e config -- consistent, not a discrepancy (4800 used here as the datasheet's own headline figure). MIG: up to 7 instances @ 18GB each.

_sources.memory_bus_width_bits: H200 NVL Product Brief (PB-12128-001_v01), Table 2-2 -- bus width figure stated for H200 NVL's HBM3e config, same die/memory subsystem as H200 SXM
